source.title: Efficacy and Safety of Doxepin 1 mg and 3 mg in a 12-week Sleep Laboratory and Outpatient Trial of Elderly Subjects with Chronic Primary Insomnia

confidence_rationale: Methodologically the strongest study in this pull -- randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 12 weeks, polysomnographic, n = 240 elderly -- and it decisively supports the anticholinergic-sparing half of IMPL-026's low-dose doxepin row with an explicit negative finding. Capped at 0.68 because the reported PSG outcomes are continuity measures (WASO, TST, SE), not the sleep-stage or spindle measures IMPL-026's Phase 2/3 assignment actually asserts.
failure_signatures: The trial reports continuity outcomes (WASO, total sleep time, sleep efficiency) and does not report spindle density, so IMPL-026's specific claim that low-dose doxepin 'enhances spindle density (Phase 3 compatible)' is unevidenced by its own primary citation.

Doses tested were 1 mg and 3 mg; IMPL-026 specifies the 3-6 mg Silenor range, so the upper half of the row's dose window is not covered and the muscarinic-sparing finding cannot be extrapolated to it unexamined.
The population was elderly patients with chronic primary insomnia, not patients at elevated MCI or Alzheimer's risk, so the row's disease-progression-relevant CONDITIONAL rating is not tested here.
A 12-week trial cannot speak to the multi-year exposure horizon over which IMPL-026's other rows assign their dementia-risk directions.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a 12-week randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial of doxepin 1 mg (n = 77), 3 mg (n = 82) and placebo (n = 81) in elderly chronic primary insomnia, the 3 mg dose significantly improved wake time after sleep onset, total sleep time and sleep efficiency versus placebo, sustained to Night 85, with 'no significant next-day residual effects' and 'no reports of memory impairment, complex sleep behaviors, anticholinergic effects, weight gain, or increased appetite'.
mapping.ree_translation: IMPL-026 rates low-dose doxepin 'NEUTRAL to mildly IMPROVES Phase 2/3', reasoning that below 10 mg the agent is a selective H1 antagonist with negligible muscarinic activity and therefore escapes the anticholinergic Phase 4 penalty that condemns the TCA row. This trial is the direct test of that dissociation and it passes: sedative benefit is obtained with an explicitly null anticholinergic and memory-effect profile.
mapping.mapping_caveat: IMPL-026 classifies medications by PREDICTED phase-specific pipeline disruption (INV-045 Phase 0-4). This paper measures neither phase-resolved consolidation nor any REE pipeline quantity; the mapping runs from a clinical endpoint back to a mechanism the study did not observe. Here the gap is sharp and specific: the trial establishes what low-dose doxepin does NOT do (no anticholinergic burden, no memory impairment) far better than what IMPL-026 says it DOES do (spindle enhancement, Phase 3 compatibility). The absence of harm is being read as the presence of architecture preservation, and those are not the same finding.
mapping.source_context: Human RCT, elderly chronic primary insomnia, 12 weeks, laboratory polysomnography plus outpatient subjective measures.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality is the highest in this pull on design grounds. mapping_fidelity is the binding constraint and is the reason the direction is mixed rather than supports: continuity metrics are not phase metrics. transfer_risk is low -- elderly insomnia to elderly at-MCI-risk is a short hop compared with the animal-to-human transfers elsewhere in this corpus.
